questions.q_text: Which of the following represents the correct order of atomic radii?
questions.solution: Radius decreases across a period (Be to B) and increases down a group, and Na is larger than Mg.
questions.chapter: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties
questions.topic: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

questions.q_text: The correct order of ionic radii of the isoelectronic species N3-, O2-, F- and Na+ is
questions.solution: All four have 10 electrons; as nuclear charge rises from N to Na the pull on the same electron cloud increases and size falls.
questions.chapter: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties
questions.topic: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

questions.q_text: The first ionization enthalpy of boron is lower than that of beryllium because
questions.opt_a: boron has a smaller atomic size than beryllium
questions.opt_b: beryllium has a half filled 2p subshell
questions.opt_c: the higher nuclear charge of boron increases screening of the valence electron
questions.opt_d: in boron the electron is removed from a 2p orbital, which is higher in energy and better shielded than the 2s orbital of beryllium
questions.solution: Be has the stable fully filled 2s2 configuration, whereas B loses a less penetrating 2p electron.
questions.chapter: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties
questions.topic: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

questions.q_text: Which halogen has the most negative electron gain enthalpy?
questions.solution: The very small size of F causes strong inter-electronic repulsion in its compact 2p subshell, so Cl exceeds F.
questions.chapter: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties
questions.topic: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

questions.q_text: Which of the following elements has the highest second ionization enthalpy?
questions.solution: Na+ already has the stable neon configuration, so removal of a second electron requires very high energy.
questions.chapter: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties
questions.topic: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

questions.q_text: Beryllium shows a diagonal relationship with
questions.solution: Be and Al have similar charge to radius ratio and electronegativity, hence similar chemical behaviour.
questions.chapter: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties
questions.topic: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

questions.q_text: The correct increasing order of first ionization enthalpy of O, N, F and Ne is
questions.solution: Nitrogen has the extra stable half filled 2p3 configuration, so its value exceeds that of oxygen.
questions.chapter: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties
questions.topic: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

questions.q_text: The element with atomic number 114 is placed in
questions.solution: Its valence configuration is 7s2 7p2, so it belongs to group 14 of the p-block.
questions.chapter: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties
questions.topic: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

questions.q_text: Which of the following oxides is amphoteric in nature?
questions.solution: Al2O3 reacts with acids to give Al3+ salts and with alkalies to give aluminate, so it is amphoteric.
questions.chapter: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties
questions.topic: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

questions.q_text: The electron gain enthalpy of fluorine is less negative than that of chlorine mainly because
questions.opt_a: fluorine has a lower nuclear charge than chlorine
questions.opt_b: the 2p subshell of fluorine is very compact, so the incoming electron faces greater electron-electron repulsion
questions.opt_c: fluorine has vacant d orbitals available for the added electron
questions.opt_d: chlorine is more electronegative than fluorine
questions.solution: High charge density on the small F atom repels the added electron, reducing the magnitude of the enthalpy released.
questions.chapter: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties
questions.topic: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

questions.q_text: Which of the following is the correct order of first ionization enthalpy?
questions.solution: Poor shielding by the intervening 3d electrons makes the value for Ga (579 kJ per mol) slightly higher than for Al (577 kJ per mol).
questions.chapter: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties
questions.topic: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

questions.q_text: Which of the following is the most acidic oxide?
questions.solution: Acidic character increases with the oxidation state and non-metallic character of the central atom; Cl2O7 gives the very strong acid HClO4.
questions.chapter: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties
questions.topic: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

questions.q_text: Ortho hydrogen and para hydrogen differ from each other in
questions.opt_b: the relative spins of their two nuclei
questions.opt_d: the type of bond joining the two atoms
questions.solution: In ortho hydrogen the two nuclear spins are parallel, while in para hydrogen they are antiparallel.

questions.q_text: The structure of hydrogen peroxide is best described as
questions.solution: H2O2 has an open book (skew) shape with a dihedral angle of about 111 degrees in the gas phase.

questions.q_text: The main product formed when potassium is burnt in excess of air is
questions.solution: Lithium gives the oxide and sodium the peroxide, but the large K+ ion stabilises the bulky superoxide ion, giving KO2.

questions.q_text: The correct order of hydration enthalpy of alkali metal ions is
questions.solution: Smaller ions have higher charge density and are hydrated more strongly, so hydration enthalpy decreases down the group.

questions.q_text: The correct order of bond angle in the group 15 hydrides is
questions.solution: Decreasing electronegativity of the central atom down the group reduces bond pair repulsion and hence the bond angle.

questions.q_text: Which of the following molecules has the largest bond angle?
questions.solution: CH4 has no lone pair on carbon, so it retains the ideal tetrahedral angle of 109 degrees 28 minutes.

questions.q_text: According to molecular orbital theory the bond order of the superoxide ion O2- is
questions.solution: O2- has 17 electrons, 10 bonding and 7 antibonding, so bond order = (10 - 7)/2 = 1.5.

questions.q_text: Which of the following molecules is paramagnetic in the gaseous state?
questions.solution: O2 has two unpaired electrons in the degenerate pi star 2p orbitals, while N2, F2 and C2 have all electrons paired.

questions.q_text: B2 is paramagnetic whereas C2 is diamagnetic. The reason is that
questions.opt_a: B2 has a higher bond order than C2
questions.opt_b: C2 has two unpaired electrons in the sigma 2p orbital
questions.opt_c: B2 contains one sigma and one pi bond
questions.opt_d: in B2 the last two electrons singly occupy the two degenerate pi 2p orbitals, while in C2 these orbitals are completely filled
questions.solution: For B2 and C2 the pi 2p orbitals lie below sigma 2p; B2 has 6 valence electrons giving two singly filled pi orbitals, C2 has 8 and fills them.

questions.q_text: The dipole moment of NH3 (1.46 D) is much larger than that of NF3 (0.24 D) because
questions.opt_a: in NH3 the resultant bond moment and the lone pair moment act in the same direction, while in NF3 they oppose each other
questions.opt_c: nitrogen has no lone pair in NF3
questions.opt_d: the N-F bond is essentially non-polar
questions.solution: N is more electronegative than H but less than F, so the bond moments reinforce the lone pair moment only in NH3.

questions.q_text: Which of the following molecules has zero dipole moment?
questions.solution: BF3 is symmetrical trigonal planar, so its three equal bond moments cancel completely.

questions.q_text: The hybridisation and shape of ClF3 are
questions.solution: Cl has 3 bond pairs and 2 lone pairs; the lone pairs occupy equatorial positions of the trigonal bipyramid giving a T-shape.

questions.q_text: The shape and hybridisation of XeF4 are
questions.solution: Xe has 4 bond pairs and 2 lone pairs; the lone pairs occupy trans axial sites leaving a square planar molecule.

questions.q_text: The correct order of Lewis acid strength of the boron trihalides is
questions.solution: p pi to p pi back bonding from halogen to boron is strongest in BF3, so BF3 accepts an electron pair least readily.

questions.q_text: The hybridisation of the chlorine atom in perchloric acid HClO4 is
questions.solution: Chlorine is surrounded by four oxygen atoms in a tetrahedral arrangement, so it is sp3 hybridised.

questions.q_text: Which of the following species has a bond order of 3?
questions.solution: NO+ has 14 electrons and is isoelectronic with N2, so its bond order is (10 - 4)/2 = 3.

questions.q_text: According to Fajans rules, which of the following compounds has the greatest covalent character?
questions.solution: Li+ is the smallest cation with the highest polarising power, so it distorts the chloride ion most.

questions.q_text: o-Nitrophenol is more volatile than p-nitrophenol because
questions.opt_a: o-nitrophenol has stronger intermolecular hydrogen bonding
questions.opt_c: p-nitrophenol has a higher molecular mass
questions.opt_d: o-nitrophenol has a much larger dipole moment
questions.solution: Chelation within the ortho molecule prevents intermolecular association, so it escapes into the vapour more easily.

questions.q_text: The shape of the SF4 molecule is
questions.solution: Sulphur is sp3d hybridised with 4 bond pairs and 1 equatorial lone pair, distorting the trigonal bipyramid to a see-saw.

questions.q_text: The bond angle in NH3 (107 degrees) is greater than that in NF3 (102 degrees) because
questions.opt_a: the N-H bonding pairs lie closer to nitrogen and repel each other more strongly than the N-F bonding pairs
questions.opt_b: nitrogen carries two lone pairs in NF3
questions.opt_d: fluorine forms an additional pi bond with nitrogen
questions.solution: Fluorine is more electronegative and draws the bonding pairs away from nitrogen, reducing bond pair repulsion.

questions.q_text: The carbon to oxygen bond order in the carbonate ion is
questions.solution: Four bonds (three sigma and one pi) are delocalised over three C-O linkages by resonance, giving 4/3 = 1.33.

questions.q_text: Which statement about the He2+ ion is correct?
questions.opt_a: It has a bond order of 1 and is very stable
questions.opt_b: It has a bond order of 0.5 and can exist
questions.opt_c: It has a bond order of zero and cannot exist
questions.opt_d: It has a bond order of 1.5 and is paramagnetic
questions.solution: He2+ has 3 electrons, 2 bonding and 1 antibonding, so bond order = (2 - 1)/2 = 0.5 and a weak bond is possible.

questions.q_text: The correct order of melting point of the sodium halides is
questions.solution: As the anion becomes larger from F- to I- the lattice enthalpy decreases and so does the melting point.

questions.q_text: Among B2, C2, N2, O2 and F2, the number of species that are paramagnetic is
questions.solution: Only B2 (two unpaired pi 2p electrons) and O2 (two unpaired pi star 2p electrons) are paramagnetic.

questions.q_text: The greater stability of the +1 oxidation state of thallium compared with its +3 state is explained by
questions.opt_b: its very high electron gain enthalpy
questions.solution: The 6s2 pair is poorly shielded by the intervening d and f electrons and is reluctant to take part in bonding.

questions.q_text: The number of three centre two electron bonds present in diborane is
questions.solution: B2H6 contains four normal two centre two electron terminal B-H bonds and two B-H-B bridging banana bonds.

questions.q_text: In the borax anion [B4O5(OH)4]2-, the number of boron atoms that are sp3 hybridised is
questions.solution: Two boron atoms are trigonal planar and sp2 hybridised while the other two are tetrahedral and sp3 hybridised.

questions.q_text: The correct order of the tendency to show catenation in group 14 is
questions.solution: Catenation falls sharply down the group because the element to element bond enthalpy decreases with increasing size.

questions.q_text: Carbon dioxide is a gas while silicon dioxide is a high melting solid because
questions.opt_a: CO2 is ionic while SiO2 is covalent
questions.opt_b: CO2 exists as discrete molecules with C=O double bonds whereas SiO2 is a three dimensional covalent network
questions.opt_c: silicon is more electronegative than carbon
questions.opt_d: SiO2 contains strong Si=O double bonds
questions.solution: Silicon cannot form effective p pi to p pi bonds with oxygen, so it uses four single Si-O bonds to build a giant lattice.

questions.q_text: In the dimer Al2Cl6, the hybridisation of aluminium and its coordination number are respectively
questions.solution: Two chlorine atoms bridge the units by donating lone pairs to the electron deficient aluminium, making each Al four coordinate.

questions.q_text: The number of bridging oxygen atoms (P-O-P linkages) present in the P4O10 molecule is
questions.solution: P4O10 has six P-O-P bridges along the edges of the P4 tetrahedron in addition to four terminal P=O bonds.

questions.q_text: In pyrosulphuric acid H2S2O7 the numbers of S-OH bonds, S=O bonds and S-O-S bonds are respectively
questions.solution: Oleum is built from two tetrahedral SO4 units sharing one oxygen; each sulphur carries one OH group and two S=O bonds.

questions.q_text: The correct order of thermal stability of the group 15 hydrides is
questions.solution: The element to hydrogen bond enthalpy falls as the size of the central atom increases down the group.

questions.q_text: The strongest oxidising agent among the halogens is
questions.solution: Its low bond dissociation enthalpy and the very high hydration enthalpy of F- give fluorine the most positive reduction potential.

questions.q_text: The correct order of bond dissociation enthalpy of the halogen molecules is
questions.solution: F2 is anomalously low because of strong repulsion between the lone pairs on the two very small fluorine atoms.

questions.q_text: The shape and hybridisation of the ICl4- ion are
questions.solution: Iodine has 4 bond pairs and 2 lone pairs; the lone pairs occupy opposite axial positions leaving a square planar ion.

questions.q_text: The correct order of acid strength of the oxoacids of chlorine is
questions.solution: Acid strength increases with the oxidation state of chlorine because the conjugate base is better stabilised by more oxygen atoms.

questions.q_text: Complete hydrolysis of XeF6 with excess of water gives
questions.solution: XeF6 + 3H2O gives XeO3 + 6HF, whereas partial hydrolysis stops at XeOF4 or XeO2F2.

questions.q_text: The shape and hybridisation of XeF2 are
questions.solution: Xe has 2 bond pairs and 3 lone pairs; the three lone pairs take equatorial positions leaving a linear molecule.

questions.q_text: Ozone is
questions.opt_a: linear, with bond order 2, and paramagnetic
questions.opt_b: bent, with equal O-O bonds of bond order 1.5, and diamagnetic
questions.opt_c: bent, with bond order 2, and paramagnetic
questions.opt_d: linear, with bond order 1.5, and diamagnetic
questions.solution: O3 is a resonance hybrid of two equivalent structures, so both bonds are identical with bond order 1.5 and all electrons are paired.

questions.q_text: Copper reacts with dilute nitric acid to liberate
questions.solution: Dilute HNO3 gives colourless nitric oxide, while concentrated HNO3 gives brown nitrogen dioxide.

questions.q_text: The basicity of phosphorous acid H3PO3 is
questions.solution: H3PO3 contains two P-OH groups and one P-H bond, and the hydrogen bonded directly to phosphorus is not ionisable.

questions.q_text: The ground state electronic configuration of chromium (Z = 24) is
questions.solution: The half filled 3d5 4s1 arrangement is extra stable because of symmetrical distribution and greater exchange energy.

questions.q_text: Which of the following ions is coloured in aqueous solution?
questions.solution: Cu2+ is 3d9 and undergoes d-d transitions, while the other ions have empty or completely filled d subshells.

questions.q_text: The spin only magnetic moment of the Mn2+ ion is
questions.solution: Mn2+ is 3d5 with five unpaired electrons, so mu = sqrt(5 x 7) = 5.92 BM.

questions.q_text: A transition metal ion has a spin only magnetic moment of 3.87 BM. The ion is
questions.solution: A value of 3.87 BM means three unpaired electrons, which corresponds to the 3d3 configuration of Cr3+.

questions.q_text: The highest oxidation state exhibited by manganese in its compounds is
questions.solution: Manganese has 3d5 4s2, so all seven valence electrons can be used, as in KMnO4.

questions.q_text: The number of electrons gained by one permanganate ion when it acts as an oxidant in acidic medium is
questions.solution: In acidic medium MnO4- with Mn in the +7 state is reduced to Mn2+, a change of five units.

questions.q_text: The structure of the dichromate ion Cr2O7 2- consists of
questions.opt_a: two CrO4 tetrahedra sharing an edge
questions.opt_b: two CrO6 octahedra sharing a face
questions.opt_c: two CrO4 tetrahedra sharing one corner oxygen, with a Cr-O-Cr angle of about 126 degrees
questions.opt_d: a planar ring of alternating chromium and oxygen atoms
questions.solution: Each chromium is tetrahedrally surrounded by oxygen and the two tetrahedra are joined through a single bridging oxygen atom.

questions.q_text: Zirconium and hafnium have almost identical atomic radii. This is due to
questions.solution: Poor shielding by the 4f electrons of the intervening lanthanoids cancels the expected size increase for hafnium.

questions.q_text: Ce4+ acts as a good oxidising agent in aqueous solution because
questions.opt_a: it has a half filled 4f subshell
questions.opt_b: it is readily reduced to the more common and more stable +3 state of the lanthanoids
questions.solution: The +3 state is the characteristic stable oxidation state of the lanthanoids, so Ce4+ readily accepts an electron.

questions.q_text: The spin only magnetic moment of the Gd3+ ion (Z of Gd = 64) is
questions.solution: Gd3+ is 4f7 with seven unpaired electrons, so mu = sqrt(7 x 9) = 7.94 BM.

questions.q_text: Actinoids exhibit a much larger number of oxidation states than lanthanoids because
questions.opt_a: the 5f, 6d and 7s orbitals are of comparable energy
questions.opt_c: the 5f orbitals are more deeply buried than the 4f orbitals
questions.solution: Comparable orbital energies allow electrons of all three subshells to take part in bonding.

questions.q_text: Which metal of the 3d transition series has the lowest melting point?
questions.solution: Zinc has a completely filled 3d10 subshell, so its d electrons do not contribute to metallic bonding.

questions.q_text: Which of the following pairs of ions has the same spin only magnetic moment?
questions.solution: Both Mn2+ and Fe3+ are 3d5 with five unpaired electrons, giving mu = 5.92 BM.

questions.q_text: The number of moles of KMnO4 needed to oxidise one mole of ferrous oxalate FeC2O4 completely in acidic medium is
questions.solution: One FeC2O4 releases 3 electrons (one from Fe2+ and two from oxalate) while each MnO4- accepts 5, so 3/5 = 0.6 mol is required.

questions.q_text: The IUPAC name of [Co(NH3)5Cl]Cl2 is
questions.solution: Ligands are named in alphabetical order before the metal, and the charge balance makes cobalt +3 in the cation.

questions.q_text: The oxidation state of iron in K4[Fe(CN)6] is
questions.solution: Taking 4(+1) + x + 6(-1) = 0 gives x = +2 for iron.

questions.q_text: The effective atomic number (EAN) of iron in K4[Fe(CN)6] is
questions.solution: Fe2+ has 24 electrons and six CN- ligands donate 12 more, giving 36, the atomic number of krypton.

questions.q_text: The complex ion [Ni(CN)4]2- is
questions.opt_a: square planar, dsp2 hybridised and diamagnetic
questions.opt_c: square planar, sp3 hybridised and paramagnetic
questions.solution: CN- is a strong field ligand and pairs the 3d8 electrons of Ni2+, leaving one 3d orbital free for dsp2 hybridisation.

questions.q_text: The spin only magnetic moment of [NiCl4]2- is
questions.solution: Cl- is a weak field ligand, so Ni2+ (3d8) keeps two unpaired electrons in this tetrahedral sp3 complex.

questions.q_text: [CoF6]3- is paramagnetic while [Co(NH3)6]3+ is diamagnetic. The reason is that
questions.opt_a: F- is a weak field ligand giving sp3d2 hybridisation with four unpaired electrons, while NH3 is a strong field ligand giving d2sp3 with all electrons paired
questions.opt_b: cobalt has different oxidation states in the two complexes
questions.opt_c: F- produces a larger crystal field splitting than NH3
questions.solution: Co3+ is 3d6; with weak field F- it stays high spin t2g4 eg2 with four unpaired electrons, while strong field NH3 gives t2g6.

questions.q_text: Which of the following is the strongest field ligand?
questions.solution: In the spectrochemical series CN- lies at the strong field end and produces the largest crystal field splitting.

questions.q_text: The number of geometrical isomers of [Co(NH3)4Cl2]+ is
questions.solution: An octahedral complex of the type Ma4b2 exists only as cis and trans forms.

questions.q_text: The complex ion [Co(en)3]3+ shows
questions.solution: The tris chelate is non superimposable on its mirror image, giving d and l forms, but no geometrical isomers are possible.

questions.q_text: [Co(NH3)5Br]SO4 and [Co(NH3)5SO4]Br are an example of
questions.solution: The two isomers exchange a ligand inside the coordination sphere with the counter ion, so they give different ions in solution.

questions.q_text: The ability of the NO2- ligand to bind a metal either through nitrogen or through oxygen gives rise to
questions.solution: An ambidentate ligand bonded through different donor atoms produces nitrito-N and nitrito-O linkage isomers.

questions.q_text: The EDTA4- ion acts as a
questions.solution: EDTA4- binds a metal ion through two nitrogen atoms and four carboxylate oxygen atoms.

questions.q_text: One mole of the complex CoCl3.4NH3 on treatment with excess silver nitrate solution gives
questions.solution: The compound is [Co(NH3)4Cl2]Cl, so only the single chloride ion outside the coordination sphere is precipitated.

questions.q_text: In Ni(CO)4 the oxidation state of nickel and its hybridisation are respectively
questions.solution: CO is a neutral ligand, so nickel is zero valent 3d10 4s0 and the tetrahedral carbonyl is sp3 and diamagnetic.

questions.q_text: The violet colour of the [Ti(H2O)6]3+ ion is due to
questions.opt_b: a d-d transition of the single 3d electron from t2g to eg
questions.opt_c: the presence of unpaired electrons in the 4s orbital
questions.opt_d: promotion of an electron from 3d to 4p
questions.solution: Ti3+ is 3d1 and absorbs green yellow light to promote its electron across the crystal field splitting gap.

questions.q_text: The total number of stereoisomers of [Co(en)2Cl2]+ is
questions.solution: The trans form is achiral while the cis form is chiral, giving trans plus a pair of cis enantiomers.

questions.q_text: The complex ion [MnBr4]2- has a spin only magnetic moment of 5.9 BM. Its geometry is
questions.solution: Five unpaired electrons mean high spin Mn2+ (3d5); with only four ligands this is possible only in a tetrahedral sp3 arrangement.

questions.q_text: The IUPAC name of (CH3)2CH-CH2-CH2-OH is
questions.solution: The longest chain carrying -OH has four carbons with -OH at C1 and a methyl at C3, so it is 3-methylbutan-1-ol.
questions.chapter: Organic Chemistry - Some Basic Principles and Techniques
questions.topic: Organic Chemistry - Some Basic Principles and Techniques

questions.q_text: The IUPAC name of (CH3)3C-CHO is
questions.solution: The -CHO carbon is C1; the chain is propanal with two methyl groups on C2, giving 2,2-dimethylpropanal.
questions.chapter: Organic Chemistry - Some Basic Principles and Techniques
questions.topic: Organic Chemistry - Some Basic Principles and Techniques

questions.q_text: The number of structural (chain) isomers possible for C5H12 is
questions.solution: Pentane, 2-methylbutane and 2,2-dimethylpropane are the only three isomers of C5H12.
questions.chapter: Organic Chemistry - Some Basic Principles and Techniques
questions.topic: Organic Chemistry - Some Basic Principles and Techniques

questions.q_text: The number of isomeric alcohols (including all structural isomers) with the molecular formula C4H10O is
questions.solution: Butan-1-ol, butan-2-ol, 2-methylpropan-1-ol and 2-methylpropan-2-ol are the four alcohols of C4H10O.
questions.chapter: Organic Chemistry - Some Basic Principles and Techniques
questions.topic: Organic Chemistry - Some Basic Principles and Techniques

questions.q_text: How many hyperconjugative (no-bond resonance) structures are possible for the tert-butyl carbocation?
questions.solution: (CH3)3C+ has nine alpha C-H bonds, and each can overlap with the vacant p orbital, giving nine hyperconjugative structures.
questions.chapter: Organic Chemistry - Some Basic Principles and Techniques
questions.topic: Organic Chemistry - Some Basic Principles and Techniques

questions.q_text: The correct order of stability of carbocations is
questions.solution: More alkyl groups supply electron density by +I and hyperconjugation, so tertiary carbocation is the most stable.
questions.chapter: Organic Chemistry - Some Basic Principles and Techniques
questions.topic: Organic Chemistry - Some Basic Principles and Techniques

questions.q_text: Which of the following groups exerts the strongest -I (electron withdrawing inductive) effect?
questions.solution: The order of -I effect is -NO2 > -CN > -COOH > -F > -Cl > -Br > -I; -CH3 and -OCH3 are electron releasing overall.
questions.chapter: Organic Chemistry - Some Basic Principles and Techniques
questions.topic: Organic Chemistry - Some Basic Principles and Techniques

questions.q_text: Which of the following groups shows a +M (+R, electron donating resonance) effect?
questions.solution: The oxygen lone pair of -OCH3 is delocalised into the ring (+M); -NO2, -CN and -CHO are -M groups.
questions.chapter: Organic Chemistry - Some Basic Principles and Techniques
questions.topic: Organic Chemistry - Some Basic Principles and Techniques

questions.q_text: Which of the following species is aromatic?
questions.solution: The cyclopentadienyl anion is planar and cyclic with 6 delocalised pi electrons (n = 1), satisfying Huckel's rule.
questions.chapter: Organic Chemistry - Some Basic Principles and Techniques
questions.topic: Organic Chemistry - Some Basic Principles and Techniques

questions.q_text: Which of the following does NOT show geometrical (cis-trans) isomerism?
questions.solution: In 2-methylbut-2-ene one doubly bonded carbon carries two identical methyl groups, so cis-trans forms are identical.
questions.chapter: Organic Chemistry - Some Basic Principles and Techniques
questions.topic: Organic Chemistry - Some Basic Principles and Techniques

questions.q_text: The total number of stereoisomers of 2,3-dichlorobutane is
questions.solution: The molecule has two similar chiral centres, so it gives a d,l pair plus one achiral meso form, i.e. three stereoisomers.
questions.chapter: Organic Chemistry - Some Basic Principles and Techniques
questions.topic: Organic Chemistry - Some Basic Principles and Techniques

questions.q_text: In Lassaigne's test, the presence of nitrogen in an organic compound is confirmed by the formation of
questions.solution: Sodium fusion extract gives Na4[Fe(CN)6], which with Fe3+ forms Fe4[Fe(CN)6]3, the Prussian blue colour.
questions.chapter: Organic Chemistry - Some Basic Principles and Techniques
questions.topic: Organic Chemistry - Some Basic Principles and Techniques

questions.q_text: Propene reacts with HBr in the absence of peroxide to give mainly
questions.solution: Markovnikov addition puts H on the carbon with more hydrogens, giving the more stable secondary carbocation and 2-bromopropane.

questions.q_text: An alkene of molecular formula C6H12 gives only propanone (acetone) on reductive ozonolysis. The alkene is
questions.solution: (CH3)2C=C(CH3)2 is symmetrical, so cleavage of the double bond yields two molecules of propanone only.

questions.q_text: Reductive ozonolysis of 2-methylbut-2-ene gives
questions.solution: CH3-C(CH3)=CH-CH3 cleaves to (CH3)2C=O and CH3CHO, i.e. propanone and ethanal.

questions.q_text: Wurtz reaction of an equimolar mixture of CH3Br and CH3CH2Br with sodium in dry ether gives how many different alkanes?
questions.solution: Cross and self coupling give ethane (CH3-CH3), propane (CH3-C2H5) and n-butane (C2H5-C2H5), i.e. three alkanes.

questions.q_text: Which of the following does NOT undergo the Friedel-Crafts reaction?
questions.solution: Nitrobenzene is strongly deactivated and its nitrogen also complexes with AlCl3, so Friedel-Crafts substitution fails.

questions.q_text: The correct order of acidic strength is
questions.solution: Greater s character (sp > sp2 > sp3) holds the electron pair closer to carbon, so the terminal alkyne C-H is the most acidic.

questions.q_text: Baeyer's reagent, used to test unsaturation, is
questions.solution: Cold dilute alkaline KMnO4 is decolourised by alkenes, which are converted into vicinal diols (glycols).

questions.q_text: The major product formed when 2-bromobutane is heated with alcoholic KOH is
questions.solution: Dehydrohalogenation follows Saytzeff's rule, giving the more substituted and more stable alkene, but-2-ene.

questions.q_text: The number of isomeric monochloro products (ignoring stereoisomers) obtained on free radical chlorination of 2-methylbutane is
questions.solution: 2-Methylbutane has four different types of hydrogen (C1/2-methyl are equivalent), so four monochloro isomers are formed.

questions.q_text: Toluene treated with Cl2 in the presence of UV light gives mainly
questions.opt_c: A mixture of o- and p-chlorotoluene
questions.solution: Light favours free radical substitution in the side chain giving C6H5CH2Cl, whereas Cl2/FeCl3 in the dark substitutes the ring.

questions.q_text: Propene reacts with HBr in the presence of benzoyl peroxide to give
questions.solution: The peroxide (Kharasch) effect gives anti-Markovnikov addition through the more stable secondary free radical, yielding 1-bromopropane.

questions.q_text: Kolbe's electrolysis of an aqueous solution of sodium propanoate gives
questions.solution: Anodic decarboxylation gives C2H5 radicals which dimerise to CH3CH2-CH2CH3, n-butane, along with CO2.

questions.q_text: Which of the following alkyl bromides reacts fastest by the SN2 mechanism?
questions.solution: SN2 needs backside attack, so reactivity falls with steric crowding: methyl > primary > secondary > tertiary.

questions.q_text: Which of the following alkyl bromides undergoes hydrolysis fastest by the SN1 mechanism?
questions.solution: SN1 rate depends on carbocation stability, and (CH3)3C-Br gives the most stable tertiary carbocation.

questions.q_text: An optically active alkyl halide reacting by a pure SN2 path gives a product with
questions.solution: The nucleophile attacks from the side opposite to the leaving group, so the configuration is inverted (Walden inversion).

questions.q_text: Chlorobenzene undergoes electrophilic substitution mainly at the ortho and para positions even though -Cl is deactivating because
questions.opt_a: -Cl shows -I (deactivating) but +M, which stabilises the ortho and para intermediates
questions.opt_d: Chlorine has no lone pair to donate
questions.solution: The -I effect of chlorine slows the reaction overall, while its +M effect directs the incoming electrophile to ortho and para positions.

questions.q_text: Benzenediazonium chloride treated with Cu2Cl2/HCl (Sandmeyer reaction) gives
questions.solution: The Sandmeyer reaction replaces the diazonium group by chlorine using cuprous chloride, giving chlorobenzene and N2.

questions.q_text: The Finkelstein reaction, used to prepare alkyl iodides, employs
questions.solution: R-Cl or R-Br with NaI in dry acetone gives R-I, since NaCl and NaBr are insoluble in acetone and precipitate out.

questions.q_text: Chlorobenzene is much less reactive than ethyl chloride towards nucleophilic substitution because
questions.opt_a: Chlorine is more electronegative in chlorobenzene
questions.opt_b: The C-Cl bond has partial double bond character due to resonance and is shorter and stronger
questions.opt_c: The benzene ring is electron deficient
questions.solution: Delocalisation of the chlorine lone pair into the ring gives the C-Cl bond partial double bond character, making it hard to break.

questions.q_text: Chloroform, on exposure to air and sunlight, is slowly oxidised to the poisonous gas
questions.solution: 2CHCl3 + O2 gives 2COCl2 + 2HCl; hence chloroform is stored in dark bottles filled to the brim with 1 percent ethanol added.

questions.q_text: Hydrolysis of optically active 2-bromobutane proceeding through an SN1 path gives
questions.solution: The planar carbocation intermediate is attacked equally from both faces, giving nearly equal amounts of the two enantiomers.

questions.q_text: The correct order of reactivity towards SN1 hydrolysis is
questions.opt_d: All three react at the same rate
questions.solution: SN1 rate follows carbocation stability; the diphenylmethyl cation is stabilised by two rings, the benzyl cation by only one.

questions.q_text: Neopentyl bromide, (CH3)3C-CH2-Br, though a primary halide, is extremely unreactive towards SN2 substitution because
questions.opt_b: The bulky tert-butyl group at the beta carbon sterically blocks backside attack
questions.opt_c: The C-Br bond has double bond character
questions.opt_d: Bromide is a poor leaving group here
questions.solution: The three methyl groups on the adjacent quaternary carbon shield the reaction centre, so the transition state for backside attack is very crowded.

questions.q_text: Which alcohol gives immediate turbidity with Lucas reagent (conc. HCl and anhydrous ZnCl2) at room temperature?
questions.solution: Tertiary alcohols form the stable tertiary carbocation fastest, so the insoluble chloride separates immediately.

questions.q_text: In Victor Meyer's test, a blood red colouration in the final solution indicates
questions.solution: Primary alcohols give a nitrolic acid that turns blood red with alkali; secondary give blue and tertiary give a colourless solution.

questions.q_text: Phenol heated with CHCl3 and aqueous NaOH followed by acidification (Reimer-Tiemann reaction) gives mainly
questions.solution: Dichlorocarbene attacks the ortho position of phenoxide, and hydrolysis gives 2-hydroxybenzaldehyde (salicylaldehyde).

questions.q_text: Sodium phenoxide heated with CO2 at 400 K under pressure, followed by acidification, gives
questions.solution: This is Kolbe's reaction: CO2 acts as the electrophile at the ortho position, giving 2-hydroxybenzoic acid (salicylic acid).

questions.q_text: Which of the following is the most acidic?
questions.solution: The -NO2 group withdraws electrons by -I and -M and stabilises the phenoxide ion, so 4-nitrophenol is the strongest acid listed.

questions.q_text: The best combination for preparing 2-methoxy-2-methylpropane (tert-butyl methyl ether) by Williamson synthesis is
questions.solution: The halide must be primary; a tertiary halide with an alkoxide would undergo elimination to give 2-methylpropene.

questions.q_text: Ethanol heated with excess concentrated H2SO4 at 443 K gives
questions.solution: At 443 K intramolecular dehydration dominates and gives ethene; at 413 K with excess ethanol diethyl ether is formed.

questions.q_text: Anisole (C6H5-O-CH3) on heating with HI gives
questions.solution: Iodide attacks the smaller methyl group by SN2; the aryl-oxygen bond has partial double bond character and is not cleaved.

questions.q_text: The correct order of ease of acid catalysed dehydration of alcohols is
questions.solution: Dehydration goes through a carbocation, so the alcohol giving the most stable (tertiary) carbocation dehydrates most easily.

questions.q_text: Phenol treated with bromine water gives a white precipitate of
questions.solution: Water increases ionisation to the highly activated phenoxide, so all three available ortho and para positions are brominated.

questions.q_text: Propan-1-ol treated with PCC (pyridinium chlorochromate) in dichloromethane gives
questions.solution: PCC is a mild anhydrous oxidant that stops at the aldehyde stage and does not oxidise it further to the acid.

questions.q_text: Which of the following gives a silver mirror with Tollens' reagent?
questions.solution: Only aldehydes are oxidised by ammoniacal AgNO3; propanal gives propanoate ion and metallic silver.

questions.q_text: Which of the following does NOT reduce Fehling's solution?
questions.solution: Aromatic aldehydes such as benzaldehyde do not respond to Fehling's test, although they do give a positive Tollens' test.

questions.q_text: Which of the following does NOT give the iodoform test?
questions.solution: The iodoform test needs a CH3-CO- or CH3-CH(OH)- group; pentan-3-one (diethyl ketone) has neither.

questions.q_text: Which of the following undergoes the Cannizzaro reaction with concentrated NaOH?
questions.solution: Cannizzaro disproportionation needs an aldehyde with no alpha hydrogen; benzaldehyde gives benzyl alcohol and sodium benzoate.

questions.q_text: The product formed when ethanal is treated with dilute NaOH at low temperature (aldol reaction) is
questions.solution: The carbanion of one ethanal adds to the carbonyl of another giving 3-hydroxybutanal, which on heating loses water to form but-2-enal.

questions.q_text: Which reagent converts propanone directly into propane (Clemmensen reduction)?
questions.solution: Clemmensen reduction with zinc amalgam and concentrated HCl reduces the C=O group all the way to CH2.

questions.q_text: The Wolff-Kishner reduction of a ketone to a hydrocarbon uses
questions.opt_c: NH2NH2 followed by KOH in ethylene glycol, heat
questions.solution: The hydrazone formed with hydrazine loses N2 in hot alkaline glycol, converting C=O into CH2 under basic conditions.

questions.q_text: Ethanoyl chloride is converted into ethanal by hydrogenation over
questions.opt_a: Pd supported on BaSO4 partially poisoned with sulphur or quinoline
questions.solution: This is Rosenmund reduction; the poisoned catalyst stops the reduction at the aldehyde stage.

questions.q_text: Toluene treated with chromyl chloride (CrO2Cl2) in CS2 followed by hydrolysis gives
questions.solution: In the Etard reaction the chromium complex formed at the methyl group hydrolyses to benzaldehyde.

questions.q_text: Ethanenitrile (CH3CN) treated with SnCl2/HCl followed by hydrolysis gives
questions.solution: This is Stephen's reaction: the nitrile is reduced to an aldimine which on hydrolysis gives the aldehyde.

questions.q_text: Ethanoic acid treated with Cl2 in the presence of red phosphorus, followed by hydrolysis, gives
questions.solution: In the Hell-Volhard-Zelinsky reaction the alpha hydrogen is replaced by halogen, giving chloroethanoic acid.

questions.q_text: Which of the following is the strongest acid?
questions.solution: Each electron withdrawing chlorine increases the -I effect and stabilises the carboxylate, so trichloroethanoic acid is strongest.

questions.q_text: Benzaldehyde and acetophenone warmed with dilute NaOH give, after loss of water, the cross aldol condensation product
questions.solution: The carbanion from acetophenone (the only partner with alpha hydrogen) adds to benzaldehyde and dehydration gives the chalcone C6H5-CH=CH-CO-C6H5.

questions.q_text: Which of the following gives the carbylamine (isocyanide) test with CHCl3 and alcoholic KOH?
questions.solution: Only primary amines give the offensive smelling isocyanide, R-NC; secondary and tertiary amines do not respond.

questions.q_text: Propanamide treated with Br2 and aqueous NaOH (Hofmann bromamide reaction) gives
questions.solution: The degradation gives a primary amine with one carbon less than the amide, so CH3CH2CONH2 gives CH3CH2NH2.

questions.q_text: Which of the following amines CANNOT be prepared by the Gabriel phthalimide synthesis?
questions.solution: Aryl halides do not undergo nucleophilic substitution with the phthalimide anion, so aromatic primary amines cannot be made this way.

questions.q_text: The correct order of basic strength in aqueous solution is
questions.solution: In water the combined effect of +I, solvation and steric crowding makes the secondary amine most basic and trimethylamine weaker.

questions.q_text: Aniline is a weaker base than ammonia because
questions.opt_a: Of the large size of the phenyl group
questions.opt_c: Nitrogen in aniline is sp3 hybridised
questions.opt_d: The lone pair on nitrogen is delocalised into the benzene ring
questions.solution: Resonance delocalisation of the nitrogen lone pair into the ring makes it less available for protonation.

questions.q_text: Hinsberg's reagent, used to distinguish primary, secondary and tertiary amines, is
questions.solution: C6H5SO2Cl gives an alkali soluble product with 1 degree amines, an alkali insoluble solid with 2 degree amines and no reaction with 3 degree amines.

questions.q_text: Aniline is converted into benzenediazonium chloride by NaNO2 and HCl at
questions.solution: Diazotisation is carried out at 273-278 K because the diazonium salt decomposes to phenol above this temperature.

questions.q_text: Benzenediazonium chloride coupled with phenol in mildly alkaline medium gives
questions.solution: Electrophilic coupling occurs at the para position of the activated phenol ring, giving the orange azo dye p-hydroxyazobenzene.

questions.q_text: Ethanamine reacts with nitrous acid (NaNO2/HCl) to give
questions.solution: Aliphatic primary amines give an unstable diazonium salt that immediately loses N2 to form the alcohol, with brisk effervescence.

questions.q_text: Nitration of aniline with a mixture of concentrated HNO3 and H2SO4 gives an appreciable amount of m-nitroaniline because
questions.opt_a: The -NH2 group is inherently meta directing
questions.opt_b: In the strongly acidic medium aniline is protonated to the anilinium ion, which is meta directing
questions.opt_c: Nitration always occurs at the meta position
questions.opt_d: The amino group is oxidised before nitration
questions.solution: The anilinium ion, -NH3+, is a deactivating meta director; hence the -NH2 group is protected by acetylation before nitration.

questions.q_text: Arrange the following aromatic amines in decreasing order of basic strength in aqueous solution.
questions.solution: The electron releasing -CH3 group increases the electron density on nitrogen, while the -NO2 group withdraws it strongly.

questions.q_text: The glycosidic linkage joining the two monosaccharide units in sucrose is
questions.solution: C1 of alpha-glucose is joined to C2 of beta-fructose, so both anomeric carbons are blocked and sucrose is non-reducing.

questions.q_text: Maltose consists of
questions.opt_a: Two glucose units joined by a beta-1,4 linkage
questions.opt_b: Two glucose units joined by an alpha-1,4 linkage
questions.opt_c: Glucose and fructose joined by an alpha-1,2 linkage
questions.opt_d: Glucose and galactose joined by a beta-1,4 linkage
questions.solution: Maltose is alpha-D-glucose C1 linked to C4 of a second glucose; its free anomeric carbon makes it a reducing sugar.

questions.q_text: Which polysaccharide has beta-1,4 glycosidic linkages between its glucose units?
questions.solution: Cellulose is a straight chain polymer of beta-D-glucose joined by beta-1,4 linkages, which humans cannot digest.

questions.q_text: Glucose heated with HI and red phosphorus gives n-hexane, which shows that
questions.opt_c: Glucose has a straight chain of six carbon atoms
questions.solution: Reduction of all six carbons to a continuous chain of CH2/CH3 units proves that glucose has an unbranched six carbon skeleton.

questions.q_text: The peptide linkage in proteins is
questions.solution: It is an amide bond formed between the -COOH of one amino acid and the -NH2 of the next with loss of a water molecule.

questions.q_text: Which of the following is an essential amino acid?
questions.solution: Valine cannot be synthesised in the human body and must be supplied through the diet; the others are non-essential.

questions.q_text: Deficiency of vitamin C (ascorbic acid) causes
questions.solution: Ascorbic acid deficiency causes scurvy, marked by bleeding gums; rickets is due to vitamin D and beri-beri to vitamin B1.

questions.q_text: Pernicious anaemia is caused by the deficiency of
questions.solution: Cyanocobalamin (vitamin B12) is needed for red blood cell formation, and its deficiency causes pernicious anaemia.

questions.q_text: The nitrogenous base present in RNA but absent in DNA is
questions.solution: RNA contains uracil in place of the thymine of DNA, and its sugar is ribose instead of 2-deoxyribose.

questions.q_text: A nucleotide differs from a nucleoside in that a nucleotide also contains
questions.solution: Nucleoside is base plus sugar; esterification at C5 with phosphoric acid gives the nucleotide, and these are joined by 3'-5' phosphodiester linkages.

questions.q_text: The number of moles of oxygen gas present in 5.6 L of O2 measured at STP is:
The number of significant figures in the measurement 0.00250 g is:
questions.solution: Leading zeros are not significant but the trailing zero after the decimal point is; 2, 5 and 0 give 3 significant figures.

questions.q_text: Which of the following statements about one mole of a substance is correct?
questions.opt_a: It always contains 6.022 x 10^23 elementary entities
questions.opt_b: It always occupies a volume of 22.4 L
questions.opt_c: It always has a mass of 1 g
questions.opt_d: It has the same mass as one mole of any other substance
questions.solution: One mole is defined as the amount of substance containing exactly the Avogadro number, 6.022 x 10^23, of elementary entities, whatever the substance.

questions.q_text: 4 g of NaOH is dissolved in water to make 250 mL of solution. The molarity of the solution is:
An organic compound contains 24.24% carbon, 4.04% hydrogen and 71.72% chlorine by mass. Its empirical formula is:
14 g of N2 is allowed to react with 6 g of H2 according to N2 + 3H2 gives 2NH3. The maximum mass of NH3 that can be formed is:
questions.solution: N2 = 0.5 mol needs 1.5 mol H2 but 3 mol H2 is present, so N2 is limiting; NH3 = 2 x 0.5 = 1 mol = 17 g.

questions.q_text: A solution is prepared by mixing 46 g of ethanol (C2H5OH) with 54 g of water. The mole fraction of ethanol in the solution is:
Which of the following pairs of compounds illustrates the law of multiple proportions?
questions.solution: In CO and CO2 the masses of oxygen combining with a fixed mass of carbon are in the simple whole number ratio 1 : 2.

questions.q_text: The volume of CO2 liberated at STP by the complete thermal decomposition of 10 g of CaCO3 is:
Concentrated sulphuric acid is 98% H2SO4 by mass and has a density of 1.8 g/mL. Its molarity is:
questions.solution: M = (1000 x density x mass%) / (100 x molar mass) = (1000 x 1.8 x 98)/(100 x 98) = 18 M.

questions.q_text: Complete combustion of 0.30 g of an organic compound containing only C, H and O gave 0.44 g of CO2 and 0.18 g of H2O. The empirical formula of the compound is:
Two isotopes of the same element always differ in their:
questions.solution: Isotopes have the same atomic number (protons) and similar chemical properties but different mass numbers because they contain different numbers of neutrons.

questions.q_text: If the radius of the first Bohr orbit of the hydrogen atom is 0.529 A, the radius of the third orbit is:
Taking R_H = 2.18 x 10^-18 J, the energy of the electron in the second orbit of a hydrogen atom is:
Which of the following sets of quantum numbers is NOT permissible?
questions.solution: The azimuthal quantum number l can take values only from 0 to (n - 1), so l = 3 is impossible when n = 3.

questions.q_text: The principle stating that no two electrons in an atom can have the same set of all four quantum numbers is called:
questions.solution: This is the Pauli exclusion principle, which limits an orbital to two electrons of opposite spin.

questions.q_text: The energy released when an electron in a hydrogen atom falls from n = 3 to n = 1 is (R_H = 2.18 x 10^-18 J):
The de Broglie wavelength associated with a ball of mass 1 x 10^-3 kg moving with a velocity of 6.626 m/s is (h = 6.626 x 10^-34 J s):
The energy of one photon of light of wavelength 400 nm is (h = 6.626 x 10^-34 J s, c = 3 x 10^8 m/s):
According to the (n + l) rule, the correct order of increasing energy of the following orbitals is:
questions.solution: Lower (n + l) means lower energy; for equal (n + l) the orbital with lower n is filled first, giving 4s (4) < 3d (5) < 4p (5) < 5s (5).

questions.q_text: The position of an electron (mass 9.1 x 10^-31 kg) is measured with an uncertainty of 1 x 10^-10 m. The minimum uncertainty in its velocity is about (h = 6.626 x 10^-34 J s):
The total number of electrons that can be accommodated in all the orbitals for which n + l = 5 is:
questions.solution: The allowed sets are 3d (n=3, l=2), 4p (n=4, l=1) and 5s (n=5, l=0), holding 10 + 6 + 2 = 18 electrons.

questions.q_text: Which one of the following is an intensive property of a system?
questions.solution: Intensive properties do not depend on the amount of substance; temperature is intensive while U, H and V are extensive.

questions.q_text: A system absorbs 100 J of heat and performs 40 J of work on the surroundings. The change in internal energy of the system is:
For an adiabatic process carried out on a closed system, the correct relation is:
questions.solution: In an adiabatic process no heat is exchanged, so q = 0 and the first law gives delta U = w.

questions.q_text: For which of the following gaseous reactions is delta H equal to delta U?
questions.solution: delta H = delta U + delta n(g) RT; only for H2 + I2 gives 2HI is delta n(g) = 2 - 2 = 0.

questions.q_text: An ideal gas expands from 1 L to 6 L against a constant external pressure of 2 atm. The work done by the gas is (1 L atm = 101.3 J):
questions.solution: w = -P_ext x delta V = -2 x 5 = -10 L atm = -1013 J.

questions.q_text: For the reaction N2(g) + 3H2(g) gives 2NH3(g) at 300 K, the value of (delta H - delta U) is (R = 8.314 J/K/mol):
questions.solution: delta H - delta U = delta n(g) RT = (-2)(8.314)(300) = -4988 J = -4.99 kJ.

questions.q_text: For the melting of ice at 273 K and 1 atm pressure, which of the following is correct?
questions.opt_b: delta S is positive and delta G is zero
questions.opt_c: delta S is negative and delta G is positive
questions.opt_d: delta G is negative and delta H is zero
questions.solution: At the normal melting point solid and liquid are in equilibrium, so delta G = 0; the solid to liquid change increases disorder, so delta S is positive.

questions.q_text: A reaction will be spontaneous at all temperatures if:
questions.opt_a: delta H is positive and delta S is negative
questions.opt_b: delta H is positive and delta S is positive
questions.opt_c: delta H is negative and delta S is positive
questions.opt_d: delta H is negative and delta S is negative
questions.solution: delta G = delta H - T delta S is negative at every temperature only when delta H is negative and delta S is positive.

questions.q_text: Given that the enthalpy of formation of CO2(g) is -393.5 kJ/mol and the enthalpy of combustion of CO(g) is -283.0 kJ/mol, the enthalpy of formation of CO(g) is:
questions.solution: By Hess law, delta fH(CO) = delta fH(CO2) - delta cH(CO) = -393.5 - (-283.0) = -110.5 kJ/mol.

questions.q_text: The work done when 2 mol of an ideal gas expands reversibly and isothermally from 1 L to 10 L at 300 K is (R = 8.314 J/K/mol, log 10 = 1):
Using the bond enthalpies H-H = 435 kJ/mol, Cl-Cl = 240 kJ/mol and H-Cl = 430 kJ/mol, the enthalpy change for H2(g) + Cl2(g) gives 2HCl(g) is:
questions.solution: delta H = (bonds broken) - (bonds formed) = (435 + 240) - (2 x 430) = -185 kJ/mol.

questions.q_text: According to the Bronsted-Lowry concept, an acid is a substance that:
questions.solution: A Bronsted-Lowry acid is a proton donor, while a base is a proton acceptor; electron pair donation and acceptance define Lewis bases and acids.

questions.q_text: An aqueous solution of which of the following salts will have a pH greater than 7 at 298 K?
questions.solution: CH3COONa is the salt of a weak acid and a strong base; the acetate ion undergoes hydrolysis to give OH- ions, making the solution basic.

questions.q_text: On increasing the total pressure at constant temperature on the equilibrium N2(g) + 3H2(g) gives 2NH3(g), the equilibrium:
questions.opt_b: Shifts backward, producing more N2 and H2
questions.opt_d: Shifts forward and Kc also increases
questions.solution: By Le Chatelier principle an increase in pressure shifts the equilibrium towards the side with fewer moles of gas (2 mol NH3 versus 4 mol reactants); Kc is unchanged.

questions.q_text: The conjugate base of the hydrogen sulphate ion, HSO4-, is:
questions.solution: A conjugate base is formed by loss of one proton: HSO4- minus H+ gives SO4 2-.

questions.q_text: For the equilibrium PCl5(g) gives PCl3(g) + Cl2(g), Kc = 2 at 500 K. The value of Kp is (R = 0.0821 L atm/K/mol):
questions.solution: Kp = Kc (RT)^delta n with delta n = 1, so Kp = 2 x 0.0821 x 500 = 82.1.

questions.q_text: The pH of a 0.01 M solution of a weak monobasic acid having Ka = 1.0 x 10^-4 is:
questions.solution: [H+] = square root of (Ka x C) = square root of (10^-4 x 10^-2) = 10^-3 M, so pH = 3.

questions.q_text: Which of the following species acts as a Lewis acid?
questions.solution: BF3 has an incomplete octet on boron and can accept an electron pair, so it is a Lewis acid; the others are electron pair donors.

questions.q_text: The solubility of Ag2CrO4 in water at 298 K is 1 x 10^-4 mol/L. Its solubility product is:
questions.solution: For an A2B type salt Ksp = 4s^3 = 4 x (10^-4)^3 = 4 x 10^-12.

questions.q_text: A buffer solution contains sodium acetate and acetic acid in the mole ratio 10 : 1. If pKa of acetic acid is 4.74, the pH of the buffer is:
questions.solution: Henderson equation: pH = pKa + log([salt]/[acid]) = 4.74 + log 10 = 5.74.

questions.q_text: The solubility of AgCl (Ksp = 1 x 10^-10) in a 0.01 M NaCl solution is:
questions.solution: Due to the common ion effect [Cl-] = 0.01 M, so s = Ksp/[Cl-] = 10^-10/10^-2 = 1 x 10^-8 mol/L.

questions.q_text: 2 mol of HI is taken in a 1 L flask and allowed to reach equilibrium at a given temperature, where it is found to be 50% dissociated. The value of Kc for 2HI(g) gives H2(g) + I2(g) is:
The oxidation number of chromium in potassium dichromate, K2Cr2O7, is:
Which of the following species can act only as an oxidising agent and never as a reducing agent?
questions.solution: In HNO3 nitrogen is in its highest oxidation state of +5, so it can only be reduced; in the others the central atom has an intermediate oxidation state.

questions.q_text: In terms of electron transfer, oxidation is best defined as:
questions.opt_a: Loss of electrons by a species
questions.opt_b: Gain of electrons by a species
questions.opt_c: Gain of hydrogen by a species
questions.solution: Oxidation is the loss of electrons and is accompanied by an increase in oxidation number.

questions.q_text: In the reaction Zn(s) + Cu2+(aq) gives Zn2+(aq) + Cu(s), the oxidising agent is:
questions.solution: Cu2+ gains electrons and is reduced, therefore it acts as the oxidising agent.

questions.q_text: The number of electrons gained by one permanganate ion, MnO4-, when it is reduced in acidic medium is:
questions.solution: MnO4- + 8H+ + 5e- gives Mn2+ + 4H2O; manganese goes from +7 to +2, a gain of 5 electrons.

questions.q_text: The equivalent mass of KMnO4 (molar mass 158 g/mol) when it acts as an oxidant in acidic medium is:
questions.solution: n-factor in acidic medium is 5, so equivalent mass = 158/5 = 31.6 g/eq.

questions.q_text: The average oxidation number of iron in magnetite, Fe3O4, is:
questions.solution: 3x + 4(-2) = 0 gives x = +8/3, the average of one Fe(II) and two Fe(III) centres.

questions.q_text: Which of the following reactions does NOT involve any change in oxidation number?
questions.solution: The reaction of AgNO3 with NaCl is a simple double displacement (precipitation); every element keeps its oxidation number, so it is not a redox change.

questions.q_text: Which of the following reactions is an example of a disproportionation reaction?
questions.solution: In a disproportionation the same element is simultaneously oxidised and reduced; chlorine goes from 0 to -1 and to +1.

questions.q_text: The number of moles of Fe2+ ions that can be oxidised by 20 mL of 0.1 M KMnO4 solution in acidic medium is:
questions.solution: MnO4- + 5Fe2+ + 8H+ gives Mn2+ + 5Fe3+ + 4H2O; moles KMnO4 = 0.002, so Fe2+ = 5 x 0.002 = 0.01 mol.

questions.q_text: Which of the following is NOT a colligative property of a dilute solution?
questions.solution: Colligative properties depend only on the number of solute particles; optical rotation depends on the nature of the solute.

questions.q_text: The vapour pressure of a solvent decreases when a non-volatile solute is dissolved in it because:
questions.opt_a: The solute molecules also evaporate along with the solvent
questions.opt_b: The temperature of the solution decreases on mixing
questions.opt_c: Fewer solvent molecules are present at the surface to escape into the vapour phase
questions.opt_d: The solute increases the repulsion between solvent molecules
questions.solution: Non-volatile solute particles occupy part of the surface, reducing the number of solvent molecules that can escape, so the vapour pressure falls.

questions.q_text: The depression in freezing point of a 0.5 molal aqueous solution of urea is (Kf for water = 1.86 K kg/mol):
questions.solution: delta Tf = Kf x m = 1.86 x 0.5 = 0.93 K.

questions.q_text: A binary liquid mixture that shows a positive deviation from Raoult's law is:
questions.solution: Ethanol and acetone show weaker A-B interactions than A-A and B-B interactions, giving positive deviation; the others form stronger hydrogen bonds and deviate negatively.

questions.q_text: 1.8 g of glucose (molar mass 180 g/mol) is dissolved in 100 g of water. The elevation in boiling point is (Kb for water = 0.52 K kg/mol):
The osmotic pressure of a 0.1 M aqueous solution of a non-electrolyte at 300 K is (R = 0.0821 L atm/K/mol):
The Henry's law constant KH of a gas dissolved in a given liquid:
questions.opt_b: Decreases with rise in temperature, so solubility increases
questions.opt_c: Is numerically equal to the mole fraction of the gas
questions.opt_d: Increases with rise in temperature, so the solubility of the gas decreases
questions.solution: Dissolution of a gas is exothermic; a rise in temperature increases KH, and since x = p/KH the solubility of the gas falls.

questions.q_text: Which of the following concentration terms is independent of temperature?
questions.solution: Molality involves only masses of solute and solvent, which do not change with temperature, whereas the others involve volume, which expands on heating.

questions.q_text: The elevation in boiling point of a 0.1 molal aqueous NaCl solution, assuming complete dissociation, is (Kb for water = 0.52 K kg/mol):
questions.solution: delta Tb = i Kb m with i = 2, so delta Tb = 2 x 0.52 x 0.1 = 0.104 K.

questions.q_text: 1.0 g of a non-electrolyte solute dissolved in 50 g of water lowers the freezing point by 0.372 K. The molar mass of the solute is (Kf for water = 1.86 K kg/mol):
A 0.1 molal aqueous solution of a weak electrolyte AB freezes at a depression of 0.2046 K. The degree of dissociation of AB is (Kf for water = 1.86 K kg/mol):
questions.solution: Calculated delta Tf = 0.186 K, so i = 0.2046/0.186 = 1.1; for AB, i = 1 + alpha, giving alpha = 0.1 or 10%.

questions.q_text: Given E0(Zn2+/Zn) = -0.76 V and E0(Cu2+/Cu) = +0.34 V, the standard emf of the Daniell cell Zn | Zn2+ || Cu2+ | Cu is:
questions.solution: E0_cell = E0_cathode - E0_anode = 0.34 - (-0.76) = 1.10 V.

questions.q_text: In a galvanic cell, the electrode at which oxidation takes place is:
questions.opt_a: The anode, which is negatively charged
questions.opt_b: The cathode, which is negatively charged
questions.opt_c: The anode, which is positively charged
questions.opt_d: The cathode, which is positively charged
questions.solution: Oxidation always occurs at the anode; in a galvanic cell the anode is the negative terminal.

questions.q_text: When an aqueous solution of a strong electrolyte is progressively diluted:
questions.opt_a: Both conductivity and molar conductivity increase
questions.opt_b: Conductivity decreases but molar conductivity increases
questions.opt_c: Both conductivity and molar conductivity decrease
questions.opt_d: Conductivity increases but molar conductivity decreases
questions.solution: Dilution lowers the number of ions per unit volume, so conductivity falls; molar conductivity rises because the ions present are carried by a larger volume with less interionic interaction.

questions.q_text: The SI unit of molar conductivity is:
questions.solution: Molar conductivity = conductivity / concentration, giving units of S m2 mol-1.

questions.q_text: For the Daniell cell with E0_cell = 1.10 V and n = 2, the standard Gibbs energy change is (F = 96500 C):
Faraday's second law of electrolysis states that when the same quantity of electricity is passed through different electrolytes, the masses of the substances liberated are:
questions.opt_a: Directly proportional to their chemical equivalent masses
questions.opt_c: Directly proportional to their molar masses
questions.solution: For a fixed charge, mass liberated = (equivalent mass x Q)/96500, so the masses are in the ratio of the equivalent masses.

questions.q_text: The conductivity of a 0.1 M solution of an electrolyte is 0.0248 S/cm. Its molar conductivity in S cm2 mol-1 is:
questions.solution: Molar conductivity = (kappa x 1000)/C = (0.0248 x 1000)/0.1 = 248 S cm2 mol-1.

questions.q_text: Given the limiting molar conductivities (S cm2 mol-1) of HCl = 426, CH3COONa = 91 and NaCl = 126, the limiting molar conductivity of acetic acid is:
questions.solution: By Kohlrausch law, value for CH3COOH = 426 + 91 - 126 = 391 S cm2 mol-1.

questions.q_text: For the cell Zn | Zn2+ (0.1 M) || Cu2+ (0.01 M) | Cu with E0_cell = 1.10 V, the cell emf at 298 K is (use 0.0591/n log Q):
At 298 K a cell reaction involving 2 electrons has E0_cell = 0.0591 V. The equilibrium constant for the cell reaction is:
The half-life of a first order reaction whose rate constant is 6.93 x 10^-3 s-1 is:
If the rate constant of a reaction has the unit s-1, the order of that reaction must be:
questions.solution: The unit of k for an nth order reaction is mol(1-n) L(n-1) s-1; this reduces to s-1 only when n = 1.

questions.q_text: Which statement about the half-life of a first order reaction is correct?
questions.opt_a: It is directly proportional to the initial concentration
questions.opt_b: It is inversely proportional to the initial concentration
questions.opt_c: It is proportional to the square of the initial concentration
questions.opt_d: It is independent of the initial concentration
questions.solution: For a first order reaction t1/2 = 0.693/k, which contains no concentration term.

questions.q_text: For a zero order reaction, the rate of the reaction is:
questions.opt_a: Independent of the concentration of the reactant
questions.opt_b: Directly proportional to the concentration of the reactant
questions.opt_c: Proportional to the square of the concentration
questions.solution: Rate = k[A]^0 = k, so the rate stays constant until the reactant is exhausted.

questions.q_text: Molecularity of an elementary step, unlike order, is:
questions.opt_b: Always a positive whole number, since it counts the species colliding in that step
questions.opt_c: Always equal to the order of the overall complex reaction
questions.opt_d: Determined experimentally from the rate law
questions.solution: Molecularity counts the reacting species in a single elementary step, so it must be a positive whole number, while order is experimental and may be zero or fractional.

questions.q_text: The time required for 90% completion of a first order reaction with k = 2.303 x 10^-3 s-1 is:
The half-life of a first order reaction is 20 minutes. The time required for 75% of the reactant to be consumed is:
questions.solution: 75% completion corresponds to two half-lives, so t = 2 x 20 = 40 minutes.

questions.q_text: For the reaction A + B gives products, doubling [A] at constant [B] doubles the rate, while doubling [B] at constant [A] increases the rate four times. The overall order of the reaction is:
questions.solution: Rate = k[A]^1[B]^2, so the overall order = 1 + 2 = 3.
